decisions.rationale: The fall has no identified cause, so it is neither a proven overreaction nor the removal of the original obstacles: likely peak margins, capex-heavy cash conversion, a peer premium on P/E and P/FCF, and a fair value resting on the DCF alone. Good but not compelling; wait for the Nov 11 results.

The drop is driven by a real fundamental break, not an overreaction: US DAUq is falling, guidance is weak and the 10-Q adds structural traffic risks. Trailing multiples are cheap but rest on pre-erosion profits. Good business, not a compelling one until traffic stabilises; a lower price alone would not fix that.

Quality trend is genuinely strong, but the price exceeds base fair value, margins look cyclical-peak, NAV is unavailable and the Q3 results behind the 21.5% fall are unread. The probability-weighted scenarios sit below the price. Good, not compelling: AVOID, watch for an entry well below base fair value.

Quality is excellent and multiples sit below their 5y lows, but the price still exceeds mechanical base fair value and peers, and premium declines suggest the historical multiples no longer apply. Probability-weighted scenarios sit below the price. Good but not compelling: AVOID, entry price set at base fair value less the margin of safety.

Quality is exceptional, but P/E sits above its own median and peers, P/FCF is above its 5y maximum, and cash conversion has fallen for five years. Even the generous P/E-only valuation gives a base near the price, so the skew is not compelling. Good but not compelling is an AVOID; results on Nov 3 may clarify cash conversion.

Quality and cash generation are excellent, but this is near-peak, oil-driven earnings bought at 82-90% of the own-history multiple range, above base fair value. The macro overlay tilts moderately to the bear side. The skew does not justify conviction 4. Cash is acceptable; we revisit at a lower price.

Cheap on EV/EBITDA and FCF yield with a mechanical bear value above the price, but P/FCF sits inside its own range, TTM profit looks one-off-inflated, ROIC is below FY2021, and the research could not verify growth or Q3 results. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, no position.

Valuation is compelling on reported earnings, but the obstacle is an unmeasured discount-rate and currency shock with results due Nov 16, plus falling ROE/ROIC and flow-inflated FCF. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, so AVOID; revisit after the results show flows and the BRL/Selic reset is visible.

Cheap on every multiple, but margins have eroded for five years, sales are shrinking, TTM cash flow is flattered by one-offs and leverage is 3.0x. The turnaround is unproven, the next quarter is guided sharply lower and the stock has rallied into results. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, so AVOID.

Quality is excellent and the de-rating is real. But growth evidence is missing, returns and margins are drifting down, net cash is shrinking, concentration on Saudi state spending is likely, results land tomorrow and liquidity is thin. The modest base upside against a much deeper mechanical bear value is good but not compelling, so this is an AVOID with an entry price.

Quality and cash returns are real and the multiple is low, but base fair value upside is moderate, the bear value sits about as far below as base sits above, TTM cash conversion looks elevated, and the election-driven policy/BRL risk is unpriced in measurable terms. Good but not compelling: AVOID, with an entry price below base fair value.

Good but not compelling: base fair value offers little margin of safety and the DCF leg is below the price, while margins and ROIC are drifting down, the share count jump is unexplained and leadership is changing with results due Nov 3. Conviction 3 is below the buy threshold, so no position; cash is acceptable.

The drift signal is real, but the trade's edge is not clear. Reaching the 2:1 target needs an unanchored second leg from an overbought (RSI 82.6), near-max-multiple level, and an iDose reimbursement headline could gap the price through a wide stop. Good but not compelling, so we hold cash.

The setup qualifies, but the edge is thin: reward:risk barely above the minimum, a target capped by base fair value, RSI 77.7 and the stock far above its 50-day average, with a high-beta gap risk through a distant stop. Good but not compelling, so AVOID; a pullback holding above the reaction-day low would improve the plan.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the beat is low quality (pass-throughs, no 2027 guidance), RSI 74.1 and EV/EBITDA above its 5y max raise gap risk, and the 250 target is only marginally above the 2:1 minimum with no firm evidence behind it. Good but not compelling: AVOID, cash is acceptable.

The drift signal is real but rests on a relief rally, not a guidance raise. The ATR stop below the reaction-day low leaves the six-month high as the only supportable target, far short of 2:1; reaching 2:1 needs bull-case fair value. Overbought RSI and an unrepaired long-term trend add gap risk. No position.

The drift signal is valid, but the 2:1 target sits above base fair value and the 52-week high, against management's slower-Q4 and one-time-benefit warnings and an RSI of 80.9. The honest target cannot reach 2:1, so per owner rules this is an AVOID; low trade conviction, no position.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the edge is mostly spent: the move overshot the jump, RSI is overbought and the wide ATR stop forces a target beyond the 52-week high and every fair-value estimate. Reward:risk holds only on paper, so the trade's edge is not compelling. Cash is preferred.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the trade does not. RSI 76.0, the price +15.3% over its 50-day, multiples above their 5-year maximums and a 350.9 target far above the 287.00 high make reward:risk 2:1 on paper only. Good but not compelling, so no position. A pullback toward the 50-day would reset the trade.

The drift setup is valid, but the stop below the reaction-day low (403.05) needs a 593.70 target that only the bull fair value supports; an honest target at base fair value 557.23 falls short of 2:1. RSI 82.2 and a stretched gap to the 50-day add gap risk. Owner rule: no 2:1, no trade.
